To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) agent-mediated integrative bargaining, which is a type of negotiation that allows both parties to gain from the exchange, is more suitable than distributive bargaining for online retail electronic commerce because of its ability to consider the full range of product value; and (2) multi-attribute utility, distributed constraint satisfaction and conjoint analysis are three techniques that can be used for implementing agent-mediated, integrative negotiation.

agent-mediated integrative negotiations are a better approach than distributive negotiations to retail electronic commerce because they allow both parties (consumers and retailers) to benefit from the exchange.
agent-mediated integrative negotiations can improve retail electronic commerce by enabling consumers and retailers to jointly optimize their value.
